chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.
He was asked about a man who performed tamattuʿ with ʿumrah up to hajj, and he did not have a sacrificial offering, so he fasted three days in Dhū al-Ḥijjah.
Then he died after he had returned to his family, before fasting the seven days. Is it upon his guardian to make them up on his behalf? He said: I do not see any make-up duty upon him.

So this does not contradict the first report, because the command to make up the fasting in the first report was directed only to the three days. As for the seven days, it is not obligatory upon his guardian to make them up on his behalf, though it is recommended for him to make up all of them on his behalf.

key_terms.السَّبْعَةَ الْأَيَّامِ: the seven additional days of fasting after returning home
key_terms.تَمَتَّعَ: performed tamattuʿ hajj, combining ʿumrah with hajj in the prescribed form
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ: the three days of fasting observed during hajj in place of the offering
key_terms.قَضَاءً: make-up performance of an unfulfilled religious duty
key_terms.هَدْيٌ: the sacrificial offering required in tamattuʿ when applicable
key_terms.وَلِيِّهِ: his guardian or heir responsible for certain posthumous religious matters

ai.seo_question: If a pilgrim dies before completing the seven fast-days for tamattuʿ hajj, must his guardian fast on his behalf?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of a person performing tamattuʿ hajj who lacked a sacrificial offering and fasted the three required days, then died before fasting the remaining seven days after returning home. The Imam عليه السلام states that the guardian is not obligated to make up those seven days, while the compiler clarifies that making up all the fasts remains recommended.
